result.question: How did Tesla's automotive gross margin evolve over the last three fiscal years, and what drove the change?
result.answer:
**FY 2025 vs. FY 2024 drivers:**

The 10-K states that cost of automotive sales revenue decreased $5.60 billion, or 9%, in the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to 2024, due to decreased deliveries year over year and lower average cost per unit from sales mix and lower material costs, partially offset by lower fixed cost absorption and an increase in tariffs [0001628280-26-003952:item-7-p015]. Quarterly filings provide additional detail on the margin compression. In Q2 2025, automotive gross margin decreased from 18.5% to 17.2% compared to Q2 2024, primarily due to a decrease in regulatory credits revenue [0001628280-25-035806:part-i--item-2-p009]. For the six months ended June 30, 2025, automotive gross margin decreased from 18.5% to 16.8%, primarily due to lower average selling price per unit and a decrease in regulatory credits revenue [0001628280-25-035806:part-i--item-2-p009].

**FY 2024 vs. FY 2023 drivers:**

The provided evidence does not include a full-year MD&A discussion of FY 2024 vs. FY 2023 automotive gross margin drivers from the 10-K. However, quarterly 10-Q filings provide insight into the factors at play during FY 2024. Cost of automotive sales revenue in Q2 2024 decreased due to lower raw material costs, freight and duties, and higher IRA manufacturing credits, partially offset by higher costs for Cybertruck and the updated Model 3 at the Fremont factory due to temporary under-utilization of manufacturing capacity as production ramps [0001628280-24-032662:part-i--item-2-p008].

**Summary of key drivers across the three-year period:**

The persistent decline in automotive gross margin was driven by lower average selling prices per vehicle, temporary under-utilization of manufacturing capacity during production ramps (including Cybertruck and updated Model 3), and decreases in regulatory credits revenue, which were partially offset by lower raw material and material costs, higher IRA manufacturing credits, and favorable sales mix [0001628280-24-017503:part-i--item-2-p007] [0001628280-24-032662:part-i--item-2-p008] [0001628280-25-035806:part-i--item-2-p009] [0001628280-26-003952:item-7-p015].

### Retracted claims

The following claims could not be verified against their cited sources and were removed from the answer:
- Tesla's automotive gross margin declined steadily over the last three fiscal years, falling from 19.4% in FY 2023 to 18.4% in FY 2024 and further to 17.8% in FY 2025.
- Automotive gross profit declined from $16,030 million in FY 2023 to $14,197 million in FY 2024 and then to $12,361 million in FY 2025.
- In Q1 2025, automotive gross margin fell to 16.2% from 18.5% in Q1 2024.
- In Q1 2024, automotive gross margin decreased from 21.1% to 18.5% compared to Q1 2023, driven by changes in automotive sales revenue and cost of revenue as well as a decrease in regulatory credits revenue.
- In Q2 2024, automotive gross margin decreased from 19.2% to 18.5% compared to Q2 2023, driven by lower average selling price on vehicles and temporary under-utilization of manufacturing capacity during production ramps, partially offset by increases in regulatory credits revenue and lower average combined cost per unit.
